Larsson Distributors AB, a Gothenburg-based pharma distributor, is paying slowly and the trend is going the wrong way. It has four open invoices with Solvenza Trade Credit (CL03), the worst of them 25 days past due (INV001137, €69.2k), with three more due shortly, totalling ~€202.8k against a €270k credit limit. Settled history shows lateness worsening from 13 to 20 days on the last two paid invoices, and the payment review marks the trend as deteriorating. Separately, Trade Ledger reported on 20 September 2026 that multiple suppliers say the company has fallen behind on scheduled payments over the past quarter (NWSDEMO03, severity 4, unpaid_vendors, direct entity rather than via parent).

The score is 37.3, placing the buyer in the Watch band, from 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD) + 0.35 x 44.6 (news) = 37.3, with a PD of 0.2727. Payment contributes a weighted 21.7 and news a weighted 15.6. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the two streams point the same way, but the score sits close to the 35 threshold and leans heavily on a single article whose body is one sentence with no named vendors, no amounts and no company response, carried by one publication without corroboration. The article has decayed only from base 45 to 44.57 at 5 days, so as it ages the score trends toward the payment-only 21.7 and the buyer would mechanically fall into Healthy without any real improvement. The adjudicator also notes the payment component is point-in-time and does not reward the 13 to 20 day slippage, and that the vendor-arrears news and the overdue invoice file measure the same underlying behaviour, so they should be read as corroboration rather than two separate drivers. Net, this is a firm Watch with a downgrade bias.

The recommendation for Solvenza Trade Credit (LIM0029) is REDUCE: cut the current limit of €270000 to a revised €247525 to reach the level where expected loss meets the 25% appetite. That moves expected loss from €53197 to €48769 against a PD of 0.2727 versus the 0.25 target and the maximum liability constraint does not bind. Note the revised limit still sits above the €202800 currently owed, so the cut trims headroom rather than forcing a paydown. The limit was last reviewed in Aug 2024 and the payment review flags it as potentially outdated, so it should be re-underwritten rather than relied on.

An upgrade should rest on payment behaviour, not on the news item ageing out. The clearest lift would be clearing the 25-day overdue invoice INV001137 and settling the three invoices due shortly on time, reversing the 13 to 20 day slippage so the DPD reading and the deteriorating trend both improve. Reducing the ~€202.8k exposure, which is 75% of the €270k credit limit, would restore headroom to absorb further slippage. Corroboration on the vendor-arrears report — named suppliers, amounts, timeframe or a company response — would firm up or dispel the weakest part of the score, and a fresh re-underwrite of the stale Aug 2024 limit would put the exposure on current facts.
